blocker.summary: The r399 allocator double-issue is RESOLVED (r413/r414/r415). The r418-r421 shutdown hang is FIXED and LIVE-VERIFIED (r422), with automated regression coverage added (r424). Separate, not-yet-fixed discovery from r424: HEAD has never been buildable from a byte-for-byte fresh clone (native_vulkan_backend.cpp has never had Vulkan linkage in any committed CMakeLists.txt) -- named for a dedicated future cycle. r427 found the root cause of presented_frames=0/present=0: the host's own VdSwap stub (tools/materialize_native_import_stubs.py) never constructs or injects the XE_SWAP PM4 packet a real Xbox 360 kernel's VdSwap would build from its arguments -- the game itself never writes that packet, by design, matching real hardware. r428/r429 made this concrete: the front-buffer argument candidate (VdSwap's r4, word at offset +20) is now confirmed by a double-buffering pattern (alternates between exactly two fixed addresses across consecutive calls), and the actual configured offscreen present target's dimensions were queried live for the first time -- 1280x720, via NativeGuestVdService::bind_offscreen (already wired into the real runtime, native_runtime.cpp:50 -- the gap r294 had flagged is already closed). r429 designed a complete, specific fix (a 5-word XE_SWAP PM4 packet -- header, kSwapSignature, an unused-by-the-decoder placeholder, and width/height queried live from present_target_ rather than hardcoded) to be added as a NativeGuestVdService method in native_guest_vd.cpp (already tracked, not part of the flagged Vulkan backlog -- only includes native_vulkan_device.h, doesn't need to modify it), called from publish_write_address. It was deliberately NOT applied this cycle: the exact ring offset to write the packet at is not confirmed with enough certainty (ctx.r3, the cursor VdSwap receives, is documented as marking the END of already-written content, not necessarily the start of free space; the game's own 64-byte reservation via sub_821E4F88 at r30, one word before ctx.r3=r30+4, isn't fully reconciled with this) -- writing at the wrong offset risks corrupting an already-valid packet r426 confirmed exists near that cursor. Named for r430: confirm the exact write offset (capture what's already written in the 64-byte reservation at r30 before the VdSwap call, not just around the r30+4 cursor as r426 did), then apply the designed fix, rebuild, and live-verify present_count/presented_frames finally advances. The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion) remains the user's decision, untouched beyond what r422 already swept in -- reports and named tool/source changes for r413-r429 were committed individually.
